PhD - Assistant Professor in Business Computing
Want a data engineering job in 2026? Learn what companies are actually asking for.
Job postings reveal a clear pattern: employers want engineers who can write code, query data, build pipelines, and run them reliably at scale.
Here is where to focus:
↳ Python: 70.0%
The leading skill for building pipelines, automating workflows, transforming data, and developing platform utilities.
↳ SQL: 69.0%
Nearly equal to Python because every data engineer needs to query, validate, model, and optimize data.
↳ Cloud Platforms
AWS appears in 40.3% of postings, while Microsoft Azure reaches 34.3%. Cloud knowledge is now a core requirement.
↳ Apache Spark: 38.7%
A key skill for processing large datasets across distributed batch and streaming workloads.
↳ Pipeline Engineering
ETL appears in 32.4%, Apache Kafka in 24.4%, and Apache Airflow in 15.8%. Together, they cover movement, streaming, and orchestration.
↳ Modern Data Platforms
Snowflake reaches 29.2%, Amazon Redshift 21.8%, and Databricks 16.8%.
↳ Data Foundations
Data modeling appears in 26.6%, followed by NoSQL, data warehouses, data lakes, and MySQL.
↳ Production Skills
Java, Hadoop, Hive, and CI/CD still matter for enterprise systems, legacy workloads, and reliable delivery.
The roadmap is simple:
Master Python and SQL. Add cloud and Spark. Learn ETL, modeling, Kafka, and Airflow. Then prove everything through end-to-end projects.
Your resume lists skills. Your portfolio must show that you can turn raw data into reliable business value.
✍🏻 Ashish Joshi
